program: Political Transformation in Nepal: Candidate Selection and Electoral Consequences
description: Examines how candidate selection processes shape political inclusion (especially for women and marginalized groups) and electoral outcomes in post-federal Nepal.
partners: Rohini Pande (Yale), Soledad Artiz Prillaman (Stanford), Michael Callen (LSE)

program: Research and Evidence for Nepal's Transition (RENT)
description: Generates rigorous research and evidence to support Nepal's federal transition, analyzing effects on economic outcomes, public service delivery, and political accountability.
partners: Inclusion Economics at Yale / Economic Growth Center

description: Analyzes LISP opt-in patterns, capacity constraints, and effectiveness of local infrastructure delivery under federalism.

program: Local Governments' Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic in Nepal
description: Documents and analyzes how local governments responded to COVID-19, assessing coordination, resource deployment, and effectiveness of local-level responses.

program: Insights for Enhancing Women's Political Participation in Nepal's Local Elections
description: Generates evidence and policy insights to enhance women's political participation in local elections, examining barriers to candidacy and strategies for gender-inclusive electoral processes.

program: Coalition and Women's Political Representation in Nepal
description: Analyzes the relationship between political coalition formation and women's political representation, producing evidence for electoral reform and advocacy.

program: Strengthening Local Capacities for Disaster Risk Management
description: Strengthens local government capacity for disaster risk management, generating evidence and policy recommendations for institutional strengthening at the local level.

program: Institutional Beliefs, Civil Registration, and Service Delivery in Federal Nepal
description: Tests whether updating beliefs of local politicians and citizens about federal institutions increases equitable uptake of the digital civil registration system. Specific wards (in Lumbini and Madhesh provinces) had not yet been selected as of this data.
partners: Michael Callen (LSE), Rohini Pande (Yale), Jon Weigel (UC Berkeley), Noam Yuchtman (LSE), Zeynep Bayram (Yale)
